newsitem.title: CHINA: China sends paramilitary to village over land row.
newsitem.headline: China sends paramilitary to village over land row.

text.p: Chinese authorities have sent several hundred paramilitary armed police to restore order in a mountain village in southern Guangdong after a land dispute turned violent, local officials said on Sunday.

Officials of Jieyang city sent about 100 police troopers into Wuyun village early on Saturday and the provincial government later ordered more than 500 paramilitary People's Armed Police into the village to restore order, one local official said.

The unrest erupted in the mountain village about 325 km (195 miles) east of the Guangdong provincial capital of Guangzhou when authorities of neighbouring Jieyang city sent a work team into Wuyun to take over management of the village from the local government, said the official who declined to be identified.
Violent demonstrations erupted after supporters of the ousted local government officials protested against the arrival of the working group, he said.
"There was a situation of no government," another local official said by telephone.
The village was now calm, he said.
